Candidate bundles, first build: one component held 67 units because units were joined through the programme root MMD-2331 and through theme epics, both hubs. Fix: a parent with more than 8 children is ignored as evidence of adjacency, theme and MCP-family links became notes and no longer join units, and a union may not exceed 8 units.

Candidate bundles, second pass: the judge returned partial for four MCP allowlist-rotation windows (ISSUE-383, 385, 386, 387). Each MCP window needs its own rotation (audit-harness.md, STALE rule), so they must not merge. Fix: an MCP rotation counts as a solo member next to destructive windows (rule K1). A window that starts with Merge or promotion is no longer a bundle unit, and ISSUE-519 (a merge of #1076) is a merge window, not a promotion window.

Rewrite-risk pairs, first build: 34 pairs were real-conflict on revert words in the B title alone, and every pair with strong overlap was needs-order whatever the history. Fix: P2 needs a shared subject word between the two titles, and the stale-branch proxy (B created before A merged) was replaced by exact git ancestry (A merge commit inside the history of B head, after fetching the open PR heads by SHA). 204 pairs became benign (rule P5) because A is already in the history of B.

Pair evidence, first build: the SQL-object regex captured the words if and no, and data/golden JSON files counted as source. Fix: stop words for SQL names; data/ and evals/ are class data and never deploy.

Pilot 1 pairs: 13 of 15 rows differed from the oracle because I changed the oracle (P5, P6) after I wrote the rubric and the rubric did not list them. The rubric now lists P5 and P6. Pilot 2 pairs: 8 of 15 rows differ, all by the semantic step J1b (the revert word in B names a different subject than A). The hand-check of PR#930 against PR#889 supports the judge: the changed hunks are disjoint.

Items, hand-check failure: the first full pass judged MMD-2640 zombie-close because PR #1028 (merged) names it. Live state: #1028 covers only the swap-tool env allowlist; window ISSUE-457 (10-26 21:17Z) still ships the bar-writer fix named in the same issue. Fix: done evidence now needs a PR title that shares a subject word with the item, no live window naming the ref in its summary, no open PR and no open child issue. Zombie-close fell from 40 to 31 items; MMD-2640 is now bundle-into ISSUE-457.

Items: the keyword rule for ships missed titles such as Independent review PR ..., pr-reviewer: PR ..., and test-audit tooling; the judge corrected 28 of them through J1 (stable across both runs). The rule now lists review, reviewer, verdict, audit, rubric, assertion, judge, test, plant and helper, and a candidate window must be a production window (not a promotion, merge or release tag) with at least two declared files in common.

Capacity: unplaced own-window items were first reported as 'no day within capacity' without a reason, and items with no PR all defaulted to the snapshot-feed container, which crowded it. Fix: an item with no PR gets its own pseudo-container, a proposed window may not share a start time with another production change, a daily limit of 6 production changes was added (D7), and each unplaced item lists the rules that refused its slots.

Facts build: a day-overflow ValueError in the promotion slot list was hidden because I redirected the build output; the stale facts.json from the previous build stayed on disk. I found it by reading the printed keys. Builds now run with output visible.

Facts build: after I made the repository path portable, a build run outside the checkout read an empty git file list and silently removed every declared-file overlap from the item rows (140 rows differed from the judged rows). I caught it by comparing rows with the judged inputs. facts_plan.py now refuses a tracked-file list under 500 paths.

Evening band: the contract constraint reads 20:00-23:00Z. DEPLOY.md (rule 3 and the Windows table) moves the band to 21:00-00:00Z in CST from 2026-11-01. I applied DEPLOY.md. Under the contract wording only, the 11-02 finding (ISSUE-478 at 23:07Z) would not exist. The coordinator rules.

AgentRun transient: one items run (pilot 2, run 2) ended with 'Pi node did not deliver an accepted submission: model_error (1 turns, 0 submissions)' after 6 s. I reran the identical command once and it completed. The driver now retries the identical command once and keeps the first failure in run-NN.attempt1.err. No per-item API call replaced any AgentRun.

Process slip: I started one items run in the foreground with the wrong rows file (a stale run directory), noticed the command line, killed the process and removed its output before it was read. No verdict from it is used.

Freshness: the first judged passes (tags f1 to f6, not used in this file) ran 20 to 65 minutes after the 01:41Z snapshot. This file comes from the pipeline run r1 (snapshot 02:35Z) and the partial rerun r3 (snapshot 02:56Z, after the destructive-window rule fix); rows whose input did not change kept their earlier verdicts (content-keyed reuse, see Run history). Every AgentRun input was under one hour old against its own snapshot when it ran.

Run directories: a run stopped by the load gate leaves its finished chunk files behind, and aggregate_plan.py and build_plan.py read every chunk file in a directory. A stopped pairs run contaminated a merged directory (one pair showed a verdict from the aborted run). I found it because one pair showed different verdicts in two directories built from the same source. run_plan.py now refuses a non-empty output directory, and run-sequencing.sh clears the runs of its tag first.

The first bundle rule flagged ISSUE-345 (a feed deploy that ships the purge PR #946) as destructive because its summary says purge. Hand-check against Jira showed the purge happens in ISSUE-344. The rule now needs a window that itself removes data (not a deploy-only or verify-only window). Selftest cases cover ISSUE-344, 345 and 352.
